argument_summary: Certification is supportable on the existing record only as a narrow, caveated packet. The admissible evidence supports that aggregate launch readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and deployment is limited, reversible, and monitored. The same record also shows the developer-support migration segment remains exposed, the random organization gate does not exclude it, and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. The defensible position is therefore not that rollout controls eliminate the weakness, but that certification can proceed if the audit packet explicitly discloses the limitation and preserves the monitoring and rollback commitments.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than a full block on launch. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. Here, that standard is not met for eliminating disclosure duty, because the affected segment remains exposed and the draft risk acceptance is unapproved and incomplete. But the same policy text does permit a compliant path short of escalation if the packet does not overclaim and instead records the material limitation explicitly, consistent with the release-policy requirement to disclose unresolved limitations for named launch use cases.
concessions: The developer-support migration segment is below target on API migration guidance and remains in the initial cohort.
The current rollout gate is random by organization and does not exclude the affected segment.
The existing risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the exposed developer-support migration segment.
Rollout controls, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves remove the model-card disclosure obligation on this record.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel material is relied on for the public argument.
